facts.label: Perguntar a distância
facts.sub: Pergunte Is the waterfall far from here? Entenda It is about two miles. Pergunte Can I walk there? e How long does it take on foot? Entenda tempo de patinete e bonde.

facts.label: Milhas, não quilômetros
facts.sub: Nos EUA, as placas e os mapas usam milhas. Uma milha tem cerca de um quilômetro e meio, então dez milhas são mais ou menos dezesseis quilômetros.

facts.label: Diga o tempo
facts.sub: Em vez de falar só a distância, os americanos dizem quanto tempo leva: dez minutos de carro ou quarenta minutos a pé. É a resposta mais útil para um turista.

pages.title: A day at the waterfall · 1/3
paragraphs: It is nine o’clock in a hotel in Seattle. Marco has a free day and a big plan. He wants to see a famous waterfall. Marco thinks in kilometers, but the signs here use miles. He walks to the front desk of the hotel. A receptionist named Kim smiles at him.
“Good morning! How can I help you?” says Kim. “Hi. Is the waterfall far from here?” says Marco. “Not really. It is about two miles.” says Kim.

pages.title: A day at the waterfall · 3/3
paragraphs: “Perfect. Is there a lookout near the waterfall?” says Marco. “Yes, there is! Bring water and wear good shoes.” says Kim. Marco decides to take a scooter. Kim shows him a short map of the road. The road goes down through green trees. In fifteen minutes, he hears the water. Good shoes help, so he does not get a blister. At the lookout, the waterfall is huge and white.
